title: Safe Control for Nonlinear Systems Under Faults and Attacks Via Control Barrier Functions
summary: Peer-reviewed (IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control 2025, doi 10.1109/TAC.2025.3571338). Fault-tolerant CBFs: one EKF per sensor fault pattern, each omitting that pattern's sensors, and a CBF constraint for every estimate with its own error bound. When the constraints conflict, estimates are dropped by a solution-separation-style test against pair-excluded filters, then by largest residual. Wheeled-robot sensor-attack and Boeing 747 actuator-failure case studies in simulation.
key_takeaways: Safety filter margin from a bank of fault-excluded estimators, not one covariance: the mechanism of the close-area innovation claim C (integrity-aware safety-filter margin)
Exclusion uses separation thresholds and pair-excluded filters, close to ARAIM-style subset exclusion
When no consistent set is found it drops the largest-residual estimates instead of declaring unavailable
Simulation only, ground robot and aircraft lateral dynamics; no multirotor, no range-sensor barrier

title: Control Barrier Functions for Safe CPS Under Sensor Faults and Attacks
summary: Peer-reviewed (59th IEEE CDC 2020, pp. 796-803). Conference version of fault-tolerant CBFs: keep several state estimators, each ignoring the sensors of one fault pattern, and impose a CBF constraint per estimator so the stochastic system stays safe under any single fault pattern. Earliest found statement of the fault-hypothesis-bank safety filter.
key_takeaways: Priority date for the idea of a CBF safety filter driven by fault-excluded estimator subsets is 2020
A judge can name it as prior art for any PL-margin safety filter

title: Barrier Certificate based Safe Control for LiDAR-based Systems under Sensor Faults and Attacks
summary: Preprint (arXiv, no venue confirmed). GPS plus LiDAR system: fault-tolerant estimation rebuilds the LiDAR scan from each state estimate, excludes estimates that disagree with the scan, and removes possibly compromised scan sectors; control barrier certificates then keep the vehicle safe using the remaining estimates. Simulated UAV delivery in an urban environment.
key_takeaways: Same fault-bank-to-barrier idea applied to a UAV with a LiDAR in the loop
Uses LiDAR consistency to exclude faulty position estimates, not a protection level

title: Secure Safety Filter: Towards Safe Flight Control under Sensor Attacks
summary: Peer-reviewed (IEEE/RSJ IROS 2025, doi 10.1109/IROS60139.2025.11247729). Caltech with TII Abu Dhabi. A secure state reconstructor enumerates sensor subsets over a sliding window, keeps every state consistent with at least p-s sensors under bounded noise, and inflates these plausible states into boxes; a robust CBF filter on velocity setpoints keeps all of them inside the safe set. PX4 SITL (X500, Gazebo) and Holybro X500 hardware with two flight controllers, safe set a square keep-in geofence, attacks injected on one EKF output copy. Code at github.com/tiiuae/px4-secure-state-reconstruction (no license file, checked with gh api 2026-11-09).
key_takeaways: Closest prior art to the close-area innovation claim C: multirotor, PX4, geofence margin from a fault-tolerant subset-consistency bound
Deterministic worst case over bounded noise, no probabilistic protection level or integrity risk budget
Hardware test duplicated one EKF, so sensor independence was not exercised
No range-sensor barrier, no VIO; TII is a UAE research lab

title: GNSS/INS Integration with Integrity Monitoring for UAV No-fly Zone Management
summary: Peer-reviewed (Remote Sensing 12(3):524, open access). GNSS/INS integration with an integrity layer for fault detection and exclusion and real-time horizontal protection level, aimed at keeping UAVs out of no-fly zones. Read as abstract only; whether the protection level is used as an enforcement margin in control was not confirmed.
key_takeaways: Protection level as the quantity that decides no-fly-zone compliance for a UAV
Monitoring, not a safety filter: no control law found in the abstract

title: Required Navigation Performances for Drone Flight Operations
summary: Conference paper (Engineering Proceedings 54(1):51, 2023). Proposes RNP specifications for drones from the error sources that make up total system error: path definition, flyability, autopilot envelope, positioning error and environment. Read as abstract only.
key_takeaways: Aviation already sizes containment from TSE = path definition + flight technical + navigation system error
Containment is a planning and approval margin, not a live safety filter

title: Resilient Shield: Strengthening Hivemind for Safe, Real-World Flight
summary: Company blog (news). Shield AI and Level 5 Autonomy Labs build an ASTM F3269-21 multi-monitor runtime assurance layer between Hivemind autonomy and flight control, with ground collision avoidance and well-clear monitors flight tested in 2025. The post does not say how navigation error or integrity enters the terrain or traffic margins.
key_takeaways: Commercial RTA between autonomy and autopilot exists and is being productised
No public statement that its margins come from a navigation protection level
